meta.description: Phase 3 Geometry Strategy — maps each biological element to the simplest primitive that preserves its scientifically meaningful structure. Consumed by the renderer; contains primitive TYPE assignments + preserved/not-claimed semantics + explicit geometric relationships. Dimensional numbers are REFERENCED from the 5 canonical spec files (by source param) rather than restated, except render-only widths which are marked SCHEMATIC.
meta.coordinate_system: X = longitudinal (nm), origin at Z-disc centre; YZ = transverse lattice plane.
meta.principle: Simplest geometry preserving scientifically meaningful structure. Do NOT force proteins into Platonic forms for visual consistency. Encode literature geometric relationships explicitly, not by eye. Surface polygon accuracy is secondary to topology/scale/aspect/axes/spacing/periodicity.

evidence_class_definitions.MEASURED: Read from experimental data or deposited coordinates.
evidence_class_definitions.STRONGLY INFERRED: Not measured directly, but tightly constrained by measured quantities.
evidence_class_definitions.MODELED: Computed from an explicit physical law, cited to primary literature, whose every parameter is itself MEASURED or STRONGLY INFERRED and none of which was fitted to the value being produced. Ranks BELOW 'STRONGLY INFERRED': it is a derived consequence, not an observation. Permitted only when the record declares `model_basis` (the law and its source) and `modeled_from` (the evidence class of every input). If any input is weaker than STRONGLY INFERRED, the value takes that weaker class instead, with MODELED carried as a parenthetical qualifier.
evidence_class_definitions.INFERRED: Derived by a reasonable but not tightly constraining argument.
evidence_class_definitions.SCHEMATIC: A rendering choice that is not a structural claim.
evidence_class_definitions.UNKNOWN: Not established; must be depicted as unknown rather than invented.

meta.evidence_ladder: UNKNOWN < SCHEMATIC < INFERRED < MODELED < STRONGLY INFERRED < MEASURED  (weakest to strongest; _weakest returns the lesser)

Ig_like.rationale: Ig β-sandwich fold is an elongated globular domain; a capsule preserves its ~2:1 axial:lateral aspect and axial length without implying β-strand detail. Deliberately NOT a Platonic solid.

evidence_by_claim.lateral_diameter_nm: MEASURED (mean cross-section of deposited coordinates; render width)
evidence_by_claim.aspect_ratio: STRONGLY INFERRED (literature axial length over measured cross-section; recomputed in Phase 6)

representative_structure.description: Titin domain M7, atomic-resolution single Ig domain.
representative_structure.residue_mapping_verified: EBI SIFTS pdbe/api/mappings/uniprot/3puc agrees exactly with the UniProt Q8WZ42 PDB cross-reference (33774-33871).
representative_structure.why_this_one: Highest-resolution single titin Ig domain from Homo sapiens in the PDB (0.96 A). The archetype is FOLD-generic: every titin Ig domain in this model is Pfam I-set (PF07679), so the exemplar is chosen for coordinate quality, not for its region. Its M-line location is incidental.

alternates.role: I-band exemplar — lets Phase 6 test whether folded Ig geometry is region-invariant.
I91/I27, the standard single-molecule mechanics reference domain.
alternates.caveat: SIFTS maps 12674-12765; the UniProt cross-reference lists 12680-12765. SIFTS is treated as authoritative. NMR, so no resolution figure.

representative_structure.does_not_claim: That the capsule primitive reproduces this structure's shape. No coordinate has been downloaded, measured, or fitted in Phase 5 — measurement and primitive fitting are Phase 6.

thick_filament_crown_periodicity.relationship: Myosin crowns have an approximately 14.3 nm third-order spacing; the separately measured H periodicity is 43.17 nm in the adopted source context.
thick_filament_crown_periodicity.encode_as: instanced crown markers along thick-filament cylinder at spacing = crown_axial_spacing
thick_filament_crown_periodicity.evidence_class: MEASURED (source-specific H periodicity and crown spacing)
thick_filament_crown_periodicity.not_claimed: that three rounded 14.3 nm intervals must equal every measured H periodicity exactly

titin_Aband_periodicities.relationship: The 11-domain C-zone sequence pattern, source-specific mean titin-domain spacing, derived 11-domain interval, myosin H periodicity, crown spacing, and thick-filament L periodicity are distinct quantities.
titin_Aband_periodicities.encode_as: Use the 43.78 nm arithmetic interval only for a labelled source-context C-zone display derivation; never substitute the 45.54 nm L diffraction spacing as an exact titin molecular span or register.
titin_Aband_periodicities.evidence_class: MEASURED (sequence/spacing/diffraction observations); STRONGLY INFERRED (derived interval); INFERRED (register hypothesis)
titin_Aband_periodicities.not_claimed: that 45.54 nm is an exact 11-domain titin molecular length or that any pair of these quantities is physically identical

lattice_d10_scaling.relationship: Interfilament spacing follows the constant-volume law d10 ∝ 1/sqrt(SL); d10 = sqrt(V_cell / ((2/sqrt3)·SL)). Hexagonal symmetry with myosin–actin center spacing d10/sqrt(3)·(specific factor).
lattice_d10_scaling.encode_as: computed live by GeometryEngine.latticeD10(SL); NEVER interpolated linearly.

values.rendered_d10_at_SL_2000_to_2400_nm: 41.78–38.13 (MODELED from the declared V_cell, not adopted from Irving's figure)

source_params: d10 vs sarcomere length scaling (constant-volume model)
d10 response over rat-cardiac working length

ig_domain_aspect.relationship: Folded Ig/Fn3 domains are ~4 nm axial; rendered aspect ~2:1 axial:lateral (lateral SCHEMATIC).
ig_domain_aspect.encode_as: capsule archetype length = domain axial length; lateral = render width.

defers_to.quantitative_dimensions: sarcomere.json / titin.json (never restate; reference by source)

representative_structure_selection.phase: Phase 5 step 2 — select representative experimental structures
representative_structure_selection.source_of_candidates: UniProt Q8WZ42 (TITIN_HUMAN) PDB cross-references: 64 entries. Canonical sequence length 34350 matches titin.json exactly, so cross-reference residue ranges are directly comparable to spec region spans without renumbering.
criteria_fixed_in_advance: Source organism Homo sapiens only (the sequence model is the Q8WZ42-1 reference; tissue construct review is pending).
Fold class established from Pfam annotation (PF07679/PF07654/PF07686 -> Ig_like; PF00041 -> Fn3; PF00069 -> kinase), never from the entry title.
Titin must be the subject, not an incidental component: entries with >1 polymer entity AND a genuine non-titin partner are excluded.
X-ray with a reported resolution, preferring a single domain over a tandem so the exemplar matches one archetype instance.
Rank by resolution, then by smallest residue count.
Wild-type sequence — disease/missense variant structures are not archetype exemplars.

excluded_as_complexes.5BS0: TCR/HLA-A1 complex; titin contributes a 9-residue epitope only
excluded_as_complexes.6I0Y: TnaC-stalled 50S ribosome (36 entities); titin I27 incidental

representative_structure_selection.filter_bug_found_and_fixed: An earlier pass excluded 7NIP as a complex because its Pfam PF18362 'Tri-helix bundle domain' matched a non-titin keyword hint. 7NIP has ONE entity and the tri-helix bundle IS titin's own UN2A fold. The rule now requires BOTH >1 entity AND a foreign partner.

regions_with_zero_structures.post_N2A_unknown: 0 approved structures map into residues 9852-10215, and no biological-region identity is assigned
regions_with_zero_structures.PEVK: 0 PDB cross-references map into spec span 10216-12022
regions_with_zero_structures.interpretation: PEVK receives no folded archetype. The post-N2A interval receives only a bounded zero-projection UNKNOWN ribbon. N2A is separately curated as I80-UN2A-I81-I82-I83 and depicts four generic Ig archetypes plus a non-atomic UN2A envelope whose metadata preserves the measured PDB 7NIP core and unresolved flexible flanks.

representative_structure_selection.nomenclature_caveat_UN2A: SD-01 resolves the project N2A interval as canonical Q8WZ42-1 residues 9366-9851 (I80-UN2A-I81-I82-I83). PDB 7NIP maps its UN2A core to residues 9504-9544 inside that interval but is annotated against Isoform 11; it informs UN2A identity and does not supply a Q8WZ42-1 full-region conformation. The preserved experimental I81 interval overlaps the UniProt I82 row through residue 9671, so no artificial non-overlapping boundary is claimed.
representative_structure_selection.classification_method_note: InterPro/CATH/SCOP2 annotations from RCSB proved to be whole-protein rollups IDENTICAL across every titin entry (all listing Ig, Fn3, kinase, Z-repeat, PPAK simultaneously) and therefore carry no per-entry discriminating power. Entries lacking per-entity Pfam (1TIT, 1TIU, 1WAA, 2RQ8, 7NIP) were classified instead by their SIFTS-verified residue range against the spec's own region spans.
representative_structure_selection.phase_boundary: Phase 5 SELECTS and JUSTIFIES representative structures. Downloading coordinates, extracting chains, measuring dimensions and principal axes, and fitting primitives are Phase 6 (PDB / Structural Data Pipeline). No coordinate file was downloaded or measured in Phase 5, so no archetype dimension here is derived from these structures — axial lengths remain sourced from the literature parameter in geometry_sources.json.

undepicted_declared_domains._purpose: Declared folded domains not emitted as instances. Empty after SC-20: all four curated N2A Ig domains are depicted in the composite spring and guarded by InstancingPlan.declaredVsInstanced().

adopted: lateral_diameter_nm for Ig_like, Fn3, kinase (was SCHEMATIC render width)
axial_length_nm for kinase (was absent; kinase instances emitted folded_length_nm: null)
not_adopted: axial_length_nm for Ig_like and Fn3 — remains the reviewed literature value 4.0 nm from 10.1016/j.jmb.2020.06.025
kinase long-axis orientation — N-to-C is 42.7 deg off the long axis, so no axial orientation claim is supported
measured_geometry_adoption.layout_invariance: No adopted value is read by placement code. Domain coordinates at every sarcomere length are unchanged by this adoption; only render width and the previously-null kinase folded_length_nm change.

representation_choice.Ig_like: capsule — 98.8% heavy-atom enclosure, N-to-C within 8.4 deg of the long axis, so a chain-aligned capsule is faithful
representation_choice.Fn3: capsule — 98.2% enclosure; cross-section is measurably wider than Ig
representation_choice.kinase: ellipsoid — 99.2% capsule / 97.4% ellipsoid enclosure, but the chain runs 42.7 deg off the long axis and contour length is 122 nm versus a 4.5 nm N-to-C separation, so no elongated chain-aligned primitive is warranted; an ellipsoid marks size and position only

measured_geometry_adoption.asset_export: None required. The pipeline's deliverable is a set of fitted geometric parameters, not a mesh: capsules and ellipsoids are generated procedurally in the renderer, so exporting GLB proxies would add a binary asset with no geometric information beyond these numbers. Full mmCIF files stay offline validation assets (representation level 3, load_in_browser: false).

interdomain_geometry.what_this_is: geometry BETWEEN consecutive domains, measured from tandem depositions. The per-class measurements in domain_archetypes come from single-domain entries and therefore cannot supply it.

in_situ_cross_check.description: cryo-EM human cardiac myosin filament, 6.4 A; titin Ig117-Fn73 (A-band super-repeat) in situ
deliberately_not_measured: per-domain principal axes, inter-axis bend, and azimuthal twist — a 6.4 A backbone does not support an axis fit precise enough to claim an angle

vs_crystal_and_literature.interpretation: In-situ spacing (4.102 nm, n=60, no lattice) is 0.449 nm below the crystal median (4.551 nm) and within 0.102 nm of the literature 4.0 nm axial length the spec retains. The crystal tandems are therefore not grossly packing-distorted in spacing, and the retained literature value is independently corroborated in situ.

in_situ_cross_check.why_it_matters: the crystal tandems' stated limitation is lattice packing; this entry is titin in situ on the thick filament with no lattice, so it bounds that limitation. Its spacing agrees with the retained literature axial length to within 0.11 nm, which corroborates the decision to keep the literature value driving layout.

interdomain_geometry.why_a_separate_selection: representative_structure_selection deliberately preferred 'a single domain over a tandem so the exemplar matches one archetype instance'. That is correct for per-class archetype geometry and is exactly why it cannot yield inter-domain geometry: within every selected entry all SIFTS ranges are identical, so no domain-to-domain relationship exists in the file. Tandem entries are therefore selected under the opposite criterion and used ONLY for relationships between domains, never for per-domain size.
interdomain_geometry.why_not_adopted: an Ig-Ig or Fn3-Fn3 linker is flexible; a crystal shows ONE conformation per pair, selected in part by lattice packing. A median over four independent pairs is a distribution, not a canonical value, and must not become a per-domain azimuth.

what_it_constrains.verdict: consistent: observed consecutive domains rotate by a median 163.188 deg, close to the 180 deg the policy assumes. A CONSTANT azimuth (0 deg twist) is excluded by measurement as well as by the chain-continuity argument.
what_it_constrains.policy_evidence_class_after_this: SCHEMATIC — unchanged. The measurement shows the convention is not contradicted by observed structures; it does not establish the azimuth of any individual domain in vivo.

not_claimed: a canonical inter-domain azimuth (Ig-Ig linkers are flexible; each crystal shows one conformation, influenced by lattice packing)
that these conformations are the in vivo conformations
that the measured twist should be adopted as a per-domain azimuth
inter-domain geometry for PEVK or N2A (disordered; no tandem crystal)
that centre-to-centre distance equals the spec's axial rise (rise is region span / domain count and includes linker extension under load; this is the compact-tandem crystal value)

context_depiction_policy._purpose: Explicit, auditable record of which structural details of titin's CONTEXT (myosin, actin, accessory proteins, lattice) this pass depicts and which it does not — with the major geometry recorded for EVERY entry, depicted or not, so that a deferred feature is a documented decision with its numbers already in hand rather than a gap someone must re-research. Companion to undepicted_declared_domains, which does the same for titin's own domains, and to context_measurements.json, which holds the measurements these decisions rest on.
context_depiction_policy.governing_objective: Titin is the subject. Context is depicted to the extent that it makes titin's geometry, attachment, and mechanics legible — and to the extent that omitting a standard illustration convention would itself mislead.

future_pass.name: maximally detailed view
future_pass.note: Several entries are DEFERRED rather than rejected. Their geometry is recorded here and in context_measurements.json so that pass needs no new literature work, only implementation.

admission_criteria._purpose: Every candidate structural detail of titin's CONTEXT (myosin, actin, accessory proteins) is admitted or excluded against these four tests, in order. Recorded so that a later reader can see WHY a detail is absent — an explicit auditable decision, not a silent omission or an oversight. Mirrors the intent of undepicted_declared_domains, which does the same job for titin's own domains.

tests_in_order.rule: A context detail is ADMITTED if titin's own geometry, attachment, or mechanics is misread without it. This is the primary test and it can carry a detail on its own.
tests_in_order.rationale: The project's objective is titin. Context exists to make titin legible, not for realism.

tests_in_order.test: Is it resolvable in the view it is meant to be read in?
tests_in_order.rule: Depict a periodicity only where its period exceeds ~4 screen px in that view. Below ~2 px per period a periodic feature ALIASES (moire) rather than merely looking small — it then actively misinforms, showing a beat frequency that is not in the structure.
tests_in_order.rationale: Nyquist. This is a measurement, not a taste judgement; see resolvability_table.

tests_in_order.test: Is it standard in scientific illustration?
tests_in_order.rule: A convention readers already expect is admitted at LOWER cost, because its absence is itself a distraction — a reader who expects myosin heads and sees a bare cylinder assumes the model is cruder than it is.
tests_in_order.rationale: User direction: standard illustration conventions may be included even when not strictly load-bearing.

tests_in_order.test: Does it cost more than it returns, or distract from titin?
tests_in_order.rule: Cost is measured in instanced primitives and in reviewer attention, not triangles — InstancedMesh makes triangle count a non-issue (see cost_table). A detail is DEFERRED if it would dominate the frame or require geometry the literature does not supply.
tests_in_order.rationale: Instancing changes the cost calculus; the binding constraint is visual attention.

not_a_reason_to_omit: triangle count alone — 12.5k heads and 28.9k actin subunits instance to ~5.3M triangles, which is unremarkable for one InstancedMesh draw call per class
that the detail is 'not about titin' — context that makes titin legible IS about titin

resolvability_table._purpose: Measured basis for admission test 2. Screen size of each candidate feature, per view. Computed at a 1200 px viewport width; scales linearly with viewport.
resolvability_table.key_consequence: Actin subunit rise is 1.3 px at full-sarcomere scale — BELOW the aliasing threshold. The actin crossover repeat is 17.8 px in the same view. So the thin filament's twist is depictable at context scale while its subunits are not; these are two different decisions about the same filament.

cost_table._note: Instance counts for a rings=2 lattice patch at SL 2200 nm, both half-sarcomeres. Triangle estimates assume one InstancedMesh per class.

myosin_heads.why: same bare-zone error as crown_levels_per_half_filament; recomputed as 102 levels x 6 heads x 19 filaments (rings=2)

cost_table.conclusion: Triangle count does not decide any of these. ~5.4M triangles across three instanced classes is unremarkable. The binding constraints are on-screen resolvability (test 2) and reader attention (test 4).

decisions.feature: Myosin head pairs on crowns (rod-plus-head morphology)

major_geometry.source_note: Crown spacing cross-checked against X-ray 14.3-14.4 nm (10.1085/jgp.202012713).

corrected_in_phase_7b.why_the_old_numbers_were_wrong: 110 was the whole 1600 nm filament divided by the 14.3 nm crown spacing (=111.9). That counts crowns through the BARE ZONE, which by definition carries no cross-bridges. The cross-bridge-bearing span is (1600 - 160)/2 = 720 nm per half, giving 51 levels per half and 102 per filament.
corrected_in_phase_7b.derivation: floor((thick_filament.length_X - bare_zone_center) / 2 / crown_axial_spacing_nm) + 1, with crown_axial_spacing_nm = 14.3 (the spec value the code reads), NOT the 14.44 nm measurement — see spacing_provenance.
corrected_in_phase_7b.note: ContextDetail.crownLevels DERIVES this from the spec rather than reading it here, so the spec dimensions remain the single source. These values are the expected result at SL 2200 nm, recorded so a later change is visible as a diff.

major_geometry.spacing_provenance: ContextDetail reads 14.3 nm from geometric_relationships.thick_filament_crown_periodicity (STRONGLY INFERRED, X-ray). 14.44 nm is this project's own centroid-to-centroid measurement on PDB 8G4L and is recorded for comparison ONLY. The two are not interchangeable in the level-count derivation: floor(720/14.3)+1 = 51 but floor(720/14.44)+1 = 50, so substituting the measurement silently changes the recorded count. Adopting it would be an evidence-class promotion requiring a spec edit and a re-source, not a swap here.

tests.2_resolvable: crown 6.9 px at full sarcomere, 43.3 px at A-band zoom

decisions.reasoning: Test 1 carries this on its own. Titin's three sectors and myosin's three-fold crown symmetry ARE THE SAME SYMMETRY, and each titin strand's interactions are with specific crowns (TA with CrH/CrD, few with CrT). Drawn as a bare cylinder, titin's sectoring looks like an arbitrary choice we made rather than a consequence of the filament's symmetry — which inverts the model's central claim. Test 3 reinforces: myosin heads are the single most universal element of sarcomere illustration; their absence reads as crudeness.
decisions.illustration_convention: Universal. Essentially every sarcomere figure since the 1960s draws projecting heads.
decisions.depiction_cost: Low. One instanced primitive class, reusing the existing InstancingPlan evidence-class split.

major_geometry.note: PAPER values to the IHM head-tail junction (see sources). Our own centroid-based measurement gave [29.3, 30.2, 60.4]: also unequal, also closing on 120, differing because the reference point differs. Use the paper's.
major_geometry.why_not: Rotations are unequal, so the array is a quasi-helix; the source reconstruction deliberately avoided helical averaging for this reason.

tests.2_resolvable: readable at A-band zoom and closer
tests.4_cost: a per-instance azimuth in the existing instancing matrix; no new primitive

decisions.reasoning: Admitted because it is nearly free once heads exist — an azimuth in the instance transform — and because getting it WRONG makes a positive false claim. A straight 3-start helix is the thing the field expected and did not find; drawing one would depict a superseded hypothesis as fact. Equally, the rotations must be drawn UNEQUAL: equalising them to 40 deg each would be inventing the regularity that the measurement excludes.
decisions.illustration_convention: Frequently drawn, often incorrectly as a regular helix. Being right here is cheap.
decisions.depiction_cost: Negligible — one extra angle per instance.

major_geometry.trap: The crossover is 180 deg of the LONG-PITCH helix, not the genetic helix: the unrounded mean consecutive-step rise/twist from 6KN7 give 37.091 nm. Computing it from the genetic helix gives a nonsense approximately 5.95 nm.

tests.2_resolvable: 1.3 px per subunit at full sarcomere — BELOW the 2 px aliasing threshold
tests.3_standard: yes, but usually at zoomed scale

decisions.reasoning: Fails tests 1 and 2. Titin does not bind actin along the thin filament — its I-band segment runs alongside and its only actin-proximal anchoring is at the Z-disc — so subunit detail explains nothing about titin. Worse, test 2 is a hard failure rather than a soft one: at 1.3 px per subunit the depiction would ALIAS, generating a visible beat pattern that is an artifact of sampling and not a feature of the filament. That is not 'too small to see', it is actively misinforming.
decisions.illustration_convention: Standard in molecular-scale figures, not in whole-sarcomere schematics.
decisions.depiction_cost: Moderate. Second-largest instance population in the scene.
decisions.what_a_maximal_pass_would_add: Instance actin subunits with the measured rise and twist, and expose them only below a view width of ~700 nm where the period clears 4 px.

decisions.feature: Thin filament long-pitch twist (crossover repeat, without subunits)

major_geometry.source_note: Coordinate-derived value is consistent with the approximate literature range near 36-37 nm.

tests.2_resolvable: 17.8 px per crossover at full sarcomere — 13.4x the subunit period, comfortably above threshold
tests.4_cost: a surface modulation or two-strand tube; no per-subunit instancing

decisions.reasoning: This is the finding that separates two decisions usually conflated. The thin filament's TWIST is resolvable at context scale even though its SUBUNITS are not, because the crossover period is approximately 13.5x the subunit rise. So the filament can be drawn as a twisted two-strand form carrying the coordinate-derived 37.091 nm repeat without instancing 760 subunits. Test 3 also applies: a smooth featureless rod for actin is less standard than a twisted pair.
decisions.illustration_convention: Very standard — the twisted two-strand actin ribbon is a recognised convention.

major_geometry.note: Troponin repeat 38.5 nm is deliberately INCOMMENSURATE with the 37.091 nm actin crossover; the two beat against each other. Both are in the source notes and both are correct.

context_depiction_policy.load_bearing_principle: The single most important entry is the myosin crown array. Titin's three sectors and myosin's three-fold crown symmetry are the same symmetry. Depicting the thick filament as a bare cylinder does not merely simplify — it makes titin's measured sectoring look like an arbitrary modelling choice, inverting the model's central claim about titin's placement.

items.severity: HIGH — result, not method. The depiction is geometrically wrong.
items.finding: The myosin head was drawn as a SINGLE capsule whose long axis is purely RADIAL (perpendicular to the filament axis), rooted at the backbone surface. Measuring 8G4L (12 complete myosin heavy chains carrying head+S2) shows this is wrong in three independent ways. (1) The projection is TWO segments, not one: an S2 segment of median length 26.00 nm leaving the backbone surface at 13.8 deg to the filament axis, then a motor domain whose 9.31 nm long axis lies at a further 17.0 deg. (2) The motor domain is displaced +8.78 nm ALONG the filament axis from its own head-tail junction, positive in 12 of 12 chains, so the projection is systematically tilted toward one pole rather than perpendicular. (3) The radial capsule reaches r = 7.5 + 16.0 = 23.50 nm, an envelope diameter of 47.0 nm against the MEASURED thick-filament-including-heads diameter of 32.356 nm — 45 percent too wide.
items.why_it_matters: The angled 'golf club' crossbridge is the standard depiction BECAUSE it is what the structure shows; every reference figure the user supplied draws it that way. A radial spike asserts a geometry the source structure contradicts, violates the project rule that measured quantities govern depiction, and overstates the radial footprint by enough to matter: the false 23.5 nm envelope exceeds the d10-derived thick-to-thin centre distance, so it would intersect neighbouring thin filaments in the lattice view.
items.corroboration_that_the_numbers_ARE_right: Head LENGTH (16.0 nm), heads per crown (6), crown spacing and inter-crown rotations are unaffected and remain adopted — all reproduce. The defect is orientation and topology only. All 11628 exported head instances measure exactly 16.00 x 1.60 nm, so the mesh was built exactly as specified: the specification was wrong, not the builder.
items.action: Replace the single radial capsule with the measured two-segment skeleton (S2 rod plus angled motor domain) in ContextDetail._heads and SarcomereScene._crownHeads. Add a validator check that the head envelope may not exceed the measured 32.356 nm filament-including-heads diameter.
items.raised_by: user review of the Phase 7b render against standard sarcomere depictions
items.status: RESOLVED — corrected and verified this session
items.resolution: Replaced with the measured two-segment skeleton. Both segments are placed by SIGNED median displacements from the head-tail junction (the node crown levels are defined at), not by angles: S2 runs 25.25 nm axially and +6.01 nm radially from the junction, and the motor domain then folds BACK 10.39 nm toward the Z-disc while moving -2.32 nm radially. The depiction now reaches r = 14.09 nm (envelope 28.18 nm) against the measured constraint of 32.356 nm, so it fits, where the superseded capsule was 43 percent over. Verified by re-exporting the built mesh and measuring it: all 36 crossbridges in a 100 nm window reproduce the specified segment lengths, radii and angles to within the writer's rounding.

items.title: I-band partition was mechanically unrealisable at every keyframe
items.detail: The four I-band regions are in mechanical series, so they must bear one common force. Inverting each region of the previously inferred partitions gave forces spanning 41x (contracted), 16x (resting) and 553x (stretched); extended_reference placed N2A and dist_Ig AT contour, unreachable at any finite force. stretched implied 277.5 pN, inside the regime the spec itself forbids depicting as ordinary contraction. Correcting stretched alone then made the N2A column DECREASE with stretch, which a series chain forbids.
items.resolution: The four modeled elastic partitions are re-derived by force balance over sourced development laws. SD-01 updates N2A to four 4.0 nm folded domains (16.0 nm rigid floor) in series with the 39 nm UN2A unique-sequence contour proxy. Residues 9852-10215 remain an explicit UNKNOWN zero-projection layout element excluded from the solver. Every state preserves its exact I-band total, so filament, overlap, M-line and lattice geometry remain unchanged.

every region non-decreasing in sarcomere length
N2A never shorter than the folded Ig domain it contains
titin.json resting reference agrees with the structural_states resting partition

items.raised: session 11 (post-Phase-9 review, reported by the user)
items.title: index.html rendered only its static shell, with no visible explanation
items.defect: The user reported the page showing 'nothing besides the legend and slider'. That is the signature of the ES module never executing: the panel h2 headings, the sub-text, and the bare <input type=range> are static markup and render with zero JavaScript, while the canvas and all ten JS-filled containers (presets, views, toggles, components, metrics, legend, evidence, notClaimed, notes, slReadout) stay empty. Diagnosis ruled out code defects first: the Phase 9 setComponentVisibility starts with an empty hidden set and only mutates matched objects; the importmap, node_modules/three 0.185.1 and the addons path all resolve; every method the page calls on model/viewer/viewer.sarcomere and every imported name resolves against the real classes; and building with exactly the options the page passes on first paint gives 21 drawables, 0 invisible, 0 effectively transparent, and a finite 2250 nm bbox. The real defect was that the page could not TELL the reader any of this: its only error surface is fail(), which writes into #err from inside the very module that had not run. The two ordinary causes both fail exactly this way — opening the page as a file:// URL (same-origin policy blocks both module resolution and the fetch of data/*.json) and serving from the wrong directory (404s on ./data and ./node_modules) — and both reported only to the devtools console.
items.fix: Added a boot diagnostic as a CLASSIC (non-module) script, which is load-bearing: a module cannot report its own failure to load. It detects the file:// case up front, listens for resource errors in capture phase (they do not bubble), catches unhandled rejections from the spec fetch, and writes a plain-language cause plus the correct serving commands into the visible #err box. A window.__titinBoot.ready flag set after viewer.start() arms a 6 s watchdog. Added npm run serve so the correct invocation is discoverable. Two gates added: a source gate, and a runtime gate that extracts the classic script and executes it against a fake DOM under three scenarios.
items.lesson: An error channel that lives inside the thing it reports on is not an error channel. The watchdog is armed by an explicit success signal placed AFTER viewer.start(), because a false alarm in an error channel is as damaging as a missed one — it teaches the reader to ignore it — and a signal placed before start() would mask a failure in start() itself. Both failure modes were negative-tested by reintroducing them and confirming the suite fails.
items.residual: The page could not be observed directly: this sandbox refuses socket binds (PermissionError on bind) and headless Chrome aborts, so no browser screenshot backs this up. The scene correctness evidence is headless Node, and the diagnostic evidence is a fake-DOM execution of the real extracted script. A browser check remains a Phase 11 validation item.

items.raised: session 12 (reported by the user: the boot diagnostic fired in the Claude Science artifact viewer)
items.title: index.html cannot work in any single-file viewer, because it fetches ./data and ./node_modules siblings
items.defect: The user opened index.html in the platform's artifact viewer and got the boot diagnostic's WATCHDOG branch, not its file:// branch. That distinction is the whole diagnosis: the protocol was not file:, so the page WAS being served — but served as a lone HTML file with no sibling directories, so every relative request (the import map's ./node_modules/three/... and SpecLoader's ./data/*.json) 404s. The page's development layout is correct for `npm run serve` and structurally incapable of working in a viewer that delivers one file. Prior sessions treated 'serve it over HTTP' as the complete answer; it is not, because a viewer offers no directory to serve.
items.fix: scripts/build_standalone.mjs emits titin_standalone.html: esbuild bundles the page's entry modules into ONE ordinary ES module (three r0.185.1 inlined, resolved from the same node_modules the tests run against), and the 7 spec files are embedded as a frozen object served by a reader satisfying the same fetchJson(name) contract browserReader implements — so SpecLoader is untouched. 1.51 MB, zero network requests. index.html is unchanged and remains the development entry point.
items.lesson: An earlier version of the builder hand-rolled module loading with one blob: URL per module and a custom resolver. It passed a Node simulation, but blob:-URL module graphs vary across browsers and CSP settings and none of that was verifiable here, so it was replaced with esbuild — the widely-exercised path. Preferring the ordinary mechanism over a clever one is the right trade when you cannot test the clever one.
items.residual: A derived artifact can drift from its source and would then render stale science with no indication. test/standalone.test.js (10 tests) rebuilds the file and asserts the embedded spec matches data/ byte-for-byte by checksum, that every spec file the loader requests is embedded, and that the I-band layout is identical to the served page at 1900/2200/2400/3000 nm. Never hand-edit titin_standalone.html.

items.raised: session 12 (found while auditing the bundler's own output)
items.title: String.replace's $& pattern silently spliced the page module into the middle of minified Three.js
items.status: RESOLVED — function-form replacement plus a post-build corruption assertion
items.defect: The first bundle contained a stray </script> inside its payload region. Cause: three.module.min.js contains `roughnessMapUv:$&&E(r.roughnessMap.channel)` — the minifier named a variable `$`, producing the substring `$&`. In the STRING form of String.prototype.replace, `$&` means 'insert the matched substring', so passing the assembled bundle as a replacement string re-inserted the ENTIRE original page module into the middle of Three.js. The output was 1.19 MB and looked plausible.
items.fix: Every replacement in the builder now goes through the FUNCTION form via a `lit()` helper, where '$' is an ordinary character; the reasoning is recorded in the script so it is not silently reverted. A post-build assertion fails the build if the original page module text survives anywhere in the output, and another requires every <script> to have exactly one </script>. Separately, JSON.stringify does not escape '<', so all embedded payloads escape '<' as \u003c (plus U+2028/U+2029) unconditionally, rather than relying on no source ever containing '</script>'.
items.lesson: A build step that emits a plausible-looking but corrupt artifact is worse than one that fails, because the corruption is discovered by a user rather than a test. The builder now refuses to write output it cannot vouch for.
items.residual: Any future string-form .replace() over vendor-minified code carries this hazard. The test 'the $& splice corruption never recurs' guards the specific signature.

items.raised: session 13 (user: "you can't zoom in close enough to see the myosin heads")
items.title: Near plane was a hard floor on zoom, making already-built detail unreachable
items.status: RESOLVED — near/far now derived from the current orbit distance every frame
items.defect: Viewer.frame() derived camera.near from the whole-sarcomere extent (near = framingDistance - 2*sceneRadius) and never updated it afterwards. At the default framing (fov 35, scene radius 1125 nm) that puts near at ~2052 nm, so dollying closer than 2052 nm clipped the ENTIRE scene and the structure vanished. The myosin crown array and the thin-filament long-pitch twist were built, toggleable, and correct the whole time — no amount of scrolling could reach them. No OrbitControls distance limits were set at all.
items.fix: _updateFrustum() sets near = max(0.1, 0.02 * currentOrbitDistance) and far to still clear the structure, and is called every frame before render(). controls.minDistance = 3 nm (a myosin head is ~19 nm), maxDistance = 20000 nm.
items.lesson: A structure spanning 2250 nm and a feature spanning 14.3 nm cannot share one fixed frustum. Deriving the depth range once, from the widest thing in the scene, silently forbids every closer scale — and the failure mode is a blank viewport, which reads as a rendering bug rather than a camera constraint.
items.evidence: test/closeup.test.js asserts every preset distance falls INSIDE the old near plane, which is the positive proof the old rule is what blocked approach, plus a frustum-intersection count (110-121 drawables) at each preset.
items.residual_risk: Verified headlessly. No browser has confirmed the depth buffer behaves as computed; z-fighting at extreme zoom remains a Phase 11 visual check.

items.title: Orbit centre is the M-line bare zone — the one place myosin heads do not exist
items.status: RESOLVED — close-up presets retarget to landmarks named from the geometry
items.defect: frame() sets controls.target to the bounding-box centre: X=1100 nm at SL=2200, which is the M-line, inside the head-free bare zone. Since a dolly moves toward the orbit target, zooming pulled the user AWAY from the myosin heads (overlap zone 300-1020 nm) and toward the one axial region that has none. This compounded P10-01: even had approach been possible, it approached nothing.
items.fix: CLOSEUPS presets each name a landmark as a FUNCTION of the geometry (overlap_zone_nm, I_A_junction_X, zdisc, mline) and closeUp() retargets there. The crown preset aims 35% into the overlap zone; the twist preset aims at the I-band side of the junction, where no thick filament occludes the helix.
items.lesson: The centroid of a periodic structure is not a useful place to look. Landmarks must be named from the biology — and because every landmark except the Z-disc origin moves (the I/A junction runs 150 -> 700 nm across the length range), they must be functions of geometry, never constants.
items.evidence: test/closeup.test.js asserts the crown view lies inside the overlap zone and explicitly NOT on the M-line at four sarcomere lengths; a separate test asserts five landmarks move >50 nm across the range while the Z-disc does not.
items.residual_risk: None known. The landmark set is not exhaustive — no preset targets the N2A or PEVK segments individually; that is Phase 10 titin-detail scope.

items.raised: session 13 (design rule, recorded so a later edit cannot quietly drop it)
items.title: Close-up spans are solved from feature size and report their own evidence
items.status: RESOLVED — spans declared per preset, distance solved from span and fov
items.defect: Not a defect. Recorded because the obvious implementation of a close-up button is a hand-tuned camera position, which breaks on a different viewport aspect and makes no claim about whether the feature is actually resolved.
items.fix: Each preset declares spanNm from the size of the feature it exists to show; distance = (spanNm / aspect / 2) / tan(fov/2). closeUp() returns the span shown and the resulting screen size of the crown spacing and the crossover repeat, so the panel displays the measurement the aliasing decision was made on.
items.lesson: A close-up is only honest if the periodicity it claims to show clears the aliasing threshold at that distance. Measured at the six presets: crown spacing 66-191 px and crossover repeat 171-494 px against a 2 px threshold. Below that the user would be shown a moire pattern and told it is a helix.
items.evidence: test/closeup.test.js — spans round-trip exactly at four aspect ratios, and a real SarcomereScene build at each preset's view width reports heads_drawn=true, twist_drawn=true, 5814 head instances.
items.residual_risk: The 2 px aliasing threshold is itself a judgement, unchanged from Phase 7b. The presets clear it by >10x so the margin is not tight.

summary.phase_7: complete as specified; three admitted features are an extension, proposed Phase 7b
summary.nothing_invalidated: No previously adopted geometry is wrong. Every item is a method gap, an un-guarded directive, or a documentation duty — not a bad number.
summary.at_phase_8_gate: All six items resolved. Three defects were found by this audit and fixed (see state_at_close.found_and_fixed_during_this_audit); four standing constraints are carried forward as rules, not tasks.

state_at_close._note: Rewritten at the Phase 8 gate and reconciled at the Phase 9 completion audit. P9-04 is closed by routing index.html through TitinVisualization for both scales. P9-05 is closed by the evidence-bearing annotation descriptor, Three.js anchor, and accessible-label implementation. P9-06 and P9-07 remain resolved standalone-build safeguards.
found_and_fixed_during_this_audit: unrealised_directives.thick_filament_crown_periodicity had become STALE: Phase 7b built crown geometry while the spec continued to declare that none existed anywhere in src/. Deleted per its own `when_realised` instruction.
The encode_as validator could not catch that, because `realised OR declared` is satisfied by the declaration alone. It now also requires the declaration to still be true.

The 4.0 deg inter-crown rotation tolerance in measure_context.py carried no recorded justification, against the project convention that a tolerance states what sets it. It is now derived: one 6.4 A resolution element at the 7 nm motor radius subtends 5.2 deg, and the published values are 16 deg apart, so 4.0 deg is inside the resolution limit while still rejecting a wrong triplet.
The interdomain pipeline consumed 8G4L SIFTS without manifesting it. 8G4L_sifts.json is now URL/byte/SHA-256 pinned and fetch_structures.py reproduces the complete 29-file cache.

The context remeasurement fitted the thin-filament axis to every polymer in 6KN7 and used median local helix steps. It now fits only actin chains and uses the global mean consecutive-step advance; the regenerated values are rise 2.755 nm, twist -166.628 deg, crossover 37.091 nm.

standing_constraints_carried_forward.cardiac_to_skeletal: 11 of the 15 context measurements are CARDIAC and marked NOT established for the model's separately declared skeletal context. They may not be adopted into skeletal geometry without skeletal evidence. This is why cMyBP-C and the measured titin azimuths stay deferred. (PH1-1)
standing_constraints_carried_forward.crown_spacing: crown_axial_spacing_nm stays at the spec's 14.3 nm. Substituting the measured 14.44 nm would make 3x disagree with the separately-sourced 43.1 nm repeat and diverge by 7.7 nm over 55 crown levels; if it is ever moved, the sources list must cite 8G4L. (PH1-2)
standing_constraints_carried_forward.milestone_4_pipeline: fit_geometry.py and generate_proxy.py are implemented and reproducible. Runtime rendering remains procedural, while the generated proxy artifact provides an auditable pipeline product. (PH6-1 closure)
standing_constraints_carried_forward.relaxed_state_tilt: The crossbridge axial tilt SIGN is a property of the relaxed interacting-heads state and does not transfer to active cross-bridges. Bears directly on Phase 8, which animates states. (PH7B-1)

unrealised_directives._purpose: geometric_relationships entries whose `encode_as` directive the renderer does NOT yet implement. Declared rather than left silent: a spec that instructs the renderer to draw something the renderer omits is the same class of defect as a spec claiming MEASURED over a schematic render. Guarded by validate_geometry.py 'Phase 3: encode_as directives'.
unrealised_directives._state: EMPTY as of Phase 7b — the crown directive it held was realised by src/geometry/ContextDetail.js and deleted per its own `when_realised` instruction. The container is retained because validate_geometry.py consults it for every encode_as directive; a future unrealised directive is declared here.

thick_filament_crown_periodicity.verified: Both distinctive tokens ('crown', 'crown_axial_spacing') appear in src/ with comments and string literals stripped, which is the same test the validator applies.
